competitors.name: Official WhatsApp Business API
competitors.notes: The official API supports catalog messages and broadcast lists natively, but requires developers to construct raw JSON payloads. No high-level library is provided by Meta.
competitors.feature_overlap: 100% feature overlap – catalog messages, broadcast lists, interactive messages.
competitors.market_positioning: The authoritative API for WhatsApp Business. Developers must build their own integration layer.

competitors.name: Twilio WhatsApp API
competitors.notes: Twilio provides a WhatsApp Business API wrapper with SDKs (Python, Node, etc.). Supports sending catalog messages via the 'catalog' message type, but broadcast list management is not exposed as a first-class feature – requires manual list handling.
competitors.feature_overlap: Catalog messages: yes. Broadcast lists: no native management, only send to a list of numbers.
competitors.market_positioning: Developer-friendly CPaaS platform, but broadcast list management is absent.

competitors.name: MessageBird WhatsApp API
competitors.notes: Offers WhatsApp Business API with catalog support. Broadcast lists are not a dedicated feature; developers must manage lists externally.
competitors.feature_overlap: Catalog messages: yes. Broadcast lists: no native management.
competitors.market_positioning: CPaaS with global reach, but lacks broadcast list abstraction.

competitors.name: WATI (WATI.io)
competitors.notes: A full WhatsApp Business API platform with built-in catalog management and broadcast campaigns. Provides a no-code interface and API for developers. Direct competitor for the use case.
competitors.feature_overlap: Catalog messages, broadcast lists, templates, automation – all native.
competitors.pricing: Starts at $49/month for basic plan, includes API access
competitors.market_positioning: All-in-one WhatsApp marketing and sales platform, targeting SMBs and mid-market.

competitors.name: Interakt (Interakt.ai)
competitors.notes: WhatsApp Business API platform with catalog sharing and broadcast campaigns. Offers API and dashboard. Direct competitor.
competitors.feature_overlap: Catalog messages, broadcast lists, templates, analytics.
competitors.market_positioning: WhatsApp commerce and engagement platform for businesses.

competitors.name: whatsapp-web.js (Open Source)
competitors.notes: Library for WhatsApp Web (not Business API). Does not support catalog messages or broadcast lists natively. Requires reverse-engineering and is against ToS. Not a viable alternative for production business use.
competitors.feature_overlap: Basic messaging only. No catalog or broadcast list support.

competitors.name: Baileys (Open Source)
competitors.notes: Another WhatsApp Web library. Similar limitations – no catalog or broadcast list support. ToS violation risk.

competitors.name: 360dialog (BSP)
competitors.notes: WhatsApp Business Solution Provider that offers API access and a dashboard. Supports catalog and broadcast features but as a managed service, not a developer library.
competitors.feature_overlap: Full catalog and broadcast support via their platform.
competitors.market_positioning: BSP for businesses wanting managed WhatsApp API.

substitutes.name: Email marketing platforms (Mailchimp, SendGrid)
substitutes.notes: Used as a workaround for product sharing and broadcasts when WhatsApp lacks native support. Not a direct competitor but a substitute for the communication channel.

substitutes.name: SMS marketing platforms (Twilio SMS, TextMagic)
substitutes.notes: Alternative channel for broadcasts, but lacks rich media catalogs.

summary: The competitive landscape for a WhatsApp API library with native catalog and broadcast list support is moderately sparse. The official WhatsApp Business API provides the underlying capabilities, but no high-level, open-source library exists that abstracts catalog messages and broadcast list management into simple function calls. Existing BSP platforms (WATI, Interakt) are full SaaS products, not libraries, and they charge monthly fees. CPaaS providers (Twilio, MessageBird) offer partial support – catalog messages are possible but broadcast list management is absent. Unofficial WhatsApp Web libraries are not viable for business use. Therefore, there is a clear gap for a lightweight, developer-friendly library that wraps the official API and provides first-class catalog and broadcast list features. The competition score is 2 because while the official API and some platforms exist, they either lack the specific abstraction or are not library-form, leaving meaningful room for a new entrant.
